data_facts_with_para.paragraph: According to the company, despite some regional challenges, in Q4, Ericsson’s sales increased by 2%, compared to last year, withNorth Americaseeing a 54% increase.

facts.fact_content: Ericsson’s sales increased by 2% in Q4 compared to last year.
North America saw a 54% increase in sales in Q4.

data_facts_with_para.paragraph: Meanwhile, overall sales for Q4 sat at SEK 72.9 billion, a slight increase from SEK 71.9 billion in Q4 2023.

facts.fact_content: Overall sales for Q4 were SEK 72.9 billion.
Overall sales increased from SEK 71.9 billion in Q4 2023 to SEK 72.9 billion.

data_facts_with_para.paragraph: The telecoms giant also reported its adjusted gross margin increased from 41.1% last year, to 46.3%, respectively, attributing better supply chain management. Cost control adjusted gross income also increased, hitting SEK 33.7 billion, up from SEK 29.6 billion last year, it stated.

facts.fact_content: Adjusted gross margin increased from 41.1% to 46.3%.
Adjusted gross income increased from SEK 29.6 billion to SEK 33.7 billion.

data_facts_with_para.paragraph: Meanwhile, Ericsson also reported a rise in free cash flow for the period, increasing from SEK 12.5 billion in 2023 to SEK 15.8 billion.

facts.fact_content: Free cash flow increased from SEK 12.5 billion to SEK 15.8 billion.

data_facts_with_para.paragraph: Net income also rose to SEK 4.9 billion, up from SEK 3.4 billion last year, the company revealed.

facts.fact_content: Net income rose from SEK 3.4 billion to SEK 4.9 billion.

data_facts_with_para.paragraph: Additionally, for the full year, Ericsson's sales dropped by 5%, mainly due to a 6% decline in Networks sales.

facts.fact_content: Ericsson's sales dropped by 5% for the full year.
Networks sales declined by 6% for the full year.

data_facts_with_para.paragraph: However, the company saw strong profit growth, with adjusted EBITA increasing to SEK 27.2 billion, up from SEK 21.4 billion in 2023.

facts.fact_content: Adjusted EBITA increased from SEK 21.4 billion to SEK 27.2 billion.
